title: 导论　历史问题　评判的时刻
originalTitle: Introduction THE HISTORICAL ISSUES A Time for Judgment

children: 马克思主义是我们这个世纪最伟大的幻想。
Marxism has been the greatest fantasy of our century.
上帝啊，我们的俄罗斯多么令人忧伤！
God, how sad our Russia is!
——亚历山大·普希金，论果戈理的《死魂灵》
And along the legendary quay Approached, not the calendar— But the real Twentieth Century.
——安娜·阿赫玛托娃，论1913年冬的圣彼得堡

zh: 苏维埃社会主义革命是现代史上最伟大的乌托邦冒险。然而，像雅努斯或俄罗斯双头鹰一样，这场实验向人类呈现出两面。对千百万人来说，它意味着社会主义的希望；对另千百万人来说，它意味着极权主义的恐怖；但对所有人来说，它都构成一种挑战，无人能置身于它的吸引力之外。七十多年间，马克思所说的“共产主义的幽灵”确实萦绕着世界。各地的人们都不得不对俄国这场实验表示赞成或反对，并以它的普世主义自负来衡量本国的政治。苏维埃幽灵因此成为20世纪政治中最大的极化力量：它赋予左派一种更严酷、更赤色的含义，并反过来使右派也极度激进化。
en: The Soviet socialist revolution was the great utopian adventure of the modern age. Yet, like Janus or the two-headed Russian eagle, this experiment offered to mankind a dual face. To millions it meant the hope of socialism, and to other millions the terror of totalitarianism; but to all it posed a challenge, and no one could escape its fascination. For over seventy years, Marx’s “spectre of Communism” in truth haunted the world. Men everywhere had to take a stand for or against the experiment in Russia and measure their domestic politics against its universalistic pretensions. The Soviet spectre thus became the great polarizing force of twentieth-century politics, giving a harsher, redder meaning to the Left and, in answer, hyperradicalizing the Right as well.

zh: 正是这场实验的正面面孔，首先使苏联事务成为全人类的事务。因为1917年十月之后，俄国不再只是另一个国家：它是世界上“第一个工人国家”，是历史上“第一个社会主义社会”。列宁的国度因此获得了普遍意义；因为完全的社会主义——而不是西方社会民主制那种不彻底的近似形式——至少在理想上，是民主平等的顶点。而在现代，谁又能反对平等呢？
en: It is the positive face of the experiment that first made the affairs of the Soviet Union the affairs of all mankind. For after October 1917, Russia was not just another country: It was the world’s “first workers’ state” and history’s “first socialist society.” The land of Lenin thus acquired universal import; for full socialism—not the half-way approximations of Western social democracy—is, at least in aspiration, the acme of democratic equality. And who, in the modern age, can be against equality?

zh: 苏维埃主义的负面面孔只是逐步显现的：无产阶级专政先变成党的专政，再变成斯大林的专政，最后，由此形成的极权体制扩张为一个全球性的、具有威胁的超级大国。在其七十年间，苏联从未作为一个普通国家融入国际体系。因此，这场实验的负面后果虽然可以用资本主义的敌意、法西斯主义和战争的压力来解释，却也提出了一个更根本——对某些人来说甚至是痛苦——的问题：苏联这个雅努斯的两副面孔，即社会主义与极权主义之间是否存在必然联系？共产主义的蜕化，是外部世界的敌意和俄国落后造成的，还是马克思列宁主义方案本身的性质造成的？这场实验变成极权主义，是
它是社会主义的，还是
它是社会主义的？
en: The negative face of Sovietism emerged only progressively, as the dictatorship of the proletariat turned first into the dictatorship of the Party and then into the dictatorship of Stalin, and finally as the resulting totalitarian system expanded into a global, threatening super-power. For throughout its seven decades the Soviet Union was never integrated into the international system as just another state. Thus, the negative consequences of the experiment, though they might be explained by the pressures of capitalist hostility, fascism, and war, also raised the more basic—and for some agonizing—question of whether there was a necessary link between the socialist and totalitarian guises of the Soviet Janus. Was the degeneration of Communism produced by the outside world’s hostility and Russian backwardness or by the nature of the Marxist-Leninist project itself? Did the experiment become totalitarian
it being socialist or
it was socialist?

zh: 随后，在与外部世界紧张对峙七十年之后，这场直到最后仍如幽灵般的实验，以现代史上最大的社会灾难告终。在没有历史先例的事件中，在四十五年和平之后，这个苏联超级大国遭受了相当于全面战争失败的结构性结局。它的脊梁——共产党——解体了；苏维埃国家本身也瓦解了；它的经济最终像1945年的德国和日本一样被夷平。事实上，这场崩溃如此彻底，以至于在不确定的未来，俄国和世界都将像当年关注这场实验的起伏一样，密切关注这场灾难的后果。
en: Then, after seven decades of tension with the external world, the experiment, spectral to the end, concluded with the greatest social disaster of the modern age. In an event without historical precedent, after forty-five years of peace the Soviet superpower suffered the structural equivalent of defeat in total war. Its backbone, the Communist Party, disintegrated; the Soviet state itself dissolved; and its economy wound up as flattened as those of Germany and Japan in 1945. Indeed, the collapse was such that Russia and the world, for an indefinite future, will be as engrossed with the consequences of the disaster as they once were with the vicissitudes of the experiment.

zh: 因此，十月革命的沉重遗产横跨——事实上划定了——安娜·阿赫玛托娃所说的“真正的二十世纪”。因为世纪并不是由整齐的百年整数日期界定的；它们是由长期的政治和文化格局界定的。欧洲的19世纪——普遍和平、经济发展和民主进步的时代——从1815年法国大革命和拿破仑危机的结束，延伸到1914年一场更广泛的世界危机的爆发。同样，人们也常说，第一次世界大战开创了我们这个阴郁的世纪。它的终止日期如今已由1989—1991年共产主义的崩溃和冷战的结束所揭示。直到那时，我们才知道我们的“短二十世纪”终于结束了。
en: The heavy heritage of October thus spans, in fact demarcates, Anna Akhmatova’s “real Twentieth Century.” For centuries are not neatly bounded by round centennial dates; rather, they are defined by long-term political and cultural patterns. Europe’s nineteenth century of general peace, economic development, and democratic progress extended from the end of the great French Revolutionary and Napoleonic crisis in 1815 to the outbreak of an even broader world crisis in 1914. Likewise it has often been asserted that the First World War inaugurated our own somber century. Its terminal date has now been revealed by the collapse of Communism and the end of the Cold War in the years 1989-1991. It was only then that we knew that our “short twentieth century” was at last over.

zh: 但这个短世纪也是一个异常暴烈和悲惨的世纪。恰如其分的是，我们这个世纪最令人着迷的意识形态的两位伟大先知——黑格尔和马克思——都把“悲剧之父”埃斯库罗斯列为最喜爱的作家。而埃斯库罗斯《奥瑞斯忒亚》的主旨是：罪行生出罪行，暴力生出暴力，直到这一链条上的第一桩罪行、这一家族的原罪，通过累积的苦难得到赎偿。类似地，正是1914年8月的鲜血，像某种阿特柔斯家族的诅咒落在现代欧洲之家，催生了主宰现代的国际暴力和社会暴力链条。因为战争的暴力和屠杀，无论对哪一方来说，都与任何可以想象的收益不相称。
en: But this short century was also an exceptionally violent and a tragic one. Appropriately, both of the great prophets of our century’s most mesmerizing ideology, Hegel and Marx, had as a favorite author the “father of tragedy,” Aeschylus. And the burden of Aeschylus’

is that crime begets crime, and violence violence, until the first crime in the chain, the original sin of the genus, is expiated through accumulated suffering. In similar fashion, it was the blood of August 1914, acting like some curse of the Atridae on the house of modern Europe, that generated the chain of international and social violence that has dominated the modern age. For the violence and carnage of the war were incommensurate with any conceivable gain, and for any party.

zh: 战争本身催生了俄国革命和布尔什维克夺取政权；其结局导致了屈辱的、复仇主义的、最终是纳粹的德国，也导致了法西斯意大利。到1930年代，这三个当时所谓的“独裁政权”已以前所未有的方式，使世界政治意识形态化和极化，同时又使大西洋西方那些受围困的宪政民主国家权力黯然失色、社会分裂。
en: The war itself produced the Russian Revolution and the Bolshevik seizure of power; its outcome led to a humiliated, revanchist, and ultimately Nazi Germany, as well as to a Fascist Italy. By the 1930s, these three “dictatorships,” as they were then called, had between them ideologized and polarized world politics in a hitherto unknown manner, while at the same time eclipsing the power and dividing the societies of the beleaguered constitutional democracies of the Atlantic West.

zh: 第二次世界大战是第一次世界大战的直接后果，并延续了这致命的螺旋。它始于希特勒试图逆转1918年的失败，但这一轮新的流血却把斯大林的权力带入欧洲心脏，同时导致共产主义在东亚的胜利，最终使列宁主义成为全球力量。这一伟大的红色突破反过来促使美国成为抗衡共产主义的力量，从而制造了又一场意识形态极化的斗争：冷战。最后，这场一触即发却非暴力的较量——一方是美国加北约，另一方是此时已具帝国形态的十月革命的继承者——持续了四十五年，直到苏联体制在压力下崩溃，交出灵魂。
en: The Second World War was a direct consequence of the First, and continued the fatal spiral. Begun as Hitler’s attempt to undo the defeat of 1918, this new round of bloodshed instead brought Stalin’s power into the heart of Europe, and at the same time led to Communist victories in East Asia, thus at last making Leninism a global force. This great Red breakthrough in turn caused the United States to become a countervailing power against Communism, thereby producing still another ideologically polarized struggle: the Cold War. Finally, this hair-trigger yet nonviolent contest between the United States-cum-NATO and the heirs to a now imperial October lasted forty-five years—until the Soviet system collapsed under the strain and gave up the ghost.

zh: 因此，在我们的百年周期结束时，在1989—1991年，1914年释放出来的复仇女神终于得到安抚。舞台因此留给了21世纪尚未为人所知的力量；无论这个世纪还将是什么样子，它至少将是后共产主义的。但可以肯定的是，后共产主义的开端将主要是努力从瓦砾堆下脱身——用亚历山大·索尔仁尼琴的比喻——清理这场实验留下的残骸。而这项任务的规模，将不亚于先前的苏维埃事业。
en: So at the end of our centenary cycle, in 1989-1991, the furies unleashed in 1914 were finally appeased. The field was thus left free for the as yet unknown forces of the twenty-first century, which, whatever else it may be, will at least be post-Communist. But what is sure is that post-Communism’s beginning will be dominated by digging out from under the rubble—to use Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn’s metaphor—left over from the experiment. And the magnitude of this task will be on a scale with the earlier Soviet endeavor.

zh: 随着我们的短二十世纪一同结束，苏联历史如今也结束了。后共产主义的俄国当然仍将是一个主要的欧洲国家和国际大国，但带有世界历史抱负的列宁主义已经完结。第一次有可能把苏联共产主义看作一个封闭的历史插曲，有清晰的开始、中间和结尾。在1989—1991年之前，我们在评估昔日的苏联之谜时，总是身处
，因此我们对苏联发展的分析受制于一系列关于实验可能如何收场的预期。如今我们知道了这场戏剧真正的结局，猜谜游戏结束了，而我们过去自以为了解的关于故事开端和中段的大部分理解，看来确实与实际相去甚远。因此，真正评估苏联冒险的过程终于可以开始：借用黑格尔的历史主义智慧，“密涅瓦的猫头鹰要到夜幕降临时才起飞。”
en: Together with our short twentieth century, Soviet history, too, is now over. Post-Communist Russia will, of course, remain a major European state and international power, but Leninism, with its world-historical pretensions, is finished. For the first time it is possible to see Soviet Communism as a closed historical episode, with a clear beginning, a middle, and an end. Until 1989-1991, in assessing the erst-while Soviet enigma, we were always somewhere

, and our analyses of Soviet development were accordingly governed by a range of expectations as to how the experiment might turn out. Now that we know the real denouement of the drama the guessing game is over, and most of what we believed we understood about the story’s beginning and middle appears far from the mark indeed. Hence, the real process of assessing the Soviet adventure can at last begin: to draw on the historicist wisdom of Hegel, “the owl of Minerva takes flight only as the shades of night are falling.”

zh: 因为苏联冒险以灾难告终，它在1917年以后的轨迹只能被理解为悲剧。十月和八月一样，都是阿特柔斯家族的诅咒：布尔什维克夺取政权的最初暴力，随着政权通过不断来自上方的强制来重塑不驯服的俄国现实，被放大了许多倍。由此产生的悲剧之所以更加完整，是因为它源于对正义、平等与和平之完美——即“社会主义”——的追求，也源于对定义“现代性”的普罗米修斯式技术力量之极致的追求。因为我们不应忘记，十月的目标不是别的，正是如马克思所说，把人类“从必然王国提升到自由王国”。我们只能在这种悖论的标志下理解苏联悲剧——需要伟大的理想，才能产生伟大的罪行。
en: Because the Soviet adventure ended in disaster, its trajectory since 1917 can be understood only as tragedy. October was just as much a curse of the Atridae as was August: The initial violence of the Bolshevik seizure of power was multiplied many times over as the regime remolded a recalcitrant Russian reality by constant coercion from above. The resulting tragedy is all the more complete because it was produced by the quest for that perfection of justice, equality, and peace which is “socialism,” and for that summum of Promethean technological power which defines “modernity.” For we should not forget that the aim of October was nothing less than to raise mankind, as Marx put it, “from the realm of necessity to the realm of freedom.” We can only understand the Soviet tragedy under the sign of this paradox—that it takes a great ideal to produce a great crime.

zh: 在走到终点之前，我们以为自己理解了苏联历史的什么？我们总是通过分析概念和范畴的滤网观察世界，这一点始终如此。但由于直接观察自我孤立的苏联如此困难，我们尤其容易像隔着昏暗的玻璃一样观看它——实际上是通过政治意识形态和社会科学方法论的双重玻璃。
en: What did we think we understood about Soviet history before we reached its end? It is always true that we observe the world through the filter of our analytical concepts and categories. But since direct observation of the self-isolated Soviet Union was so difficult, we were particularly prone to see it as through a glass darkly—indeed through a double glass of political ideology and social-science methodology.

zh: 先从后者说起。第二次世界大战后的四十五年间，西方苏联学发展成一个庞大的跨学科事业，以“价值中立”的科学自居。这项研究工作确实产生了令人印象深刻的经验成果。到1980年代末，我们已经积累了大量文献，勾勒出苏联在经济到文化各个领域的具体记录。事实上，我们如此成功，以至于在戈尔巴乔夫的
时期，苏联出版商开始翻译西方苏联学的重要著作，以帮助填补他们自己知识中的“空白点”。然而，苏联学事业的问题，在于从细节转向解释驱动苏联现实的深层动力时出了差错。
en: To begin with the latter, in the forty-five years after the Second World War, Western Sovietology grew into an enormous, multidisciplinary enterprise, operating as a “value-free” science. And this investigative effort yielded what are indeed impressive empirical results. By the end of the 1980s, we had built up a vast corpus of literature staking out the details of the Soviet record in all domains, from economics to culture. In fact, we were so successful that during Gorbachev’s

Soviet publishers took to translating key works of Western Sovietology to help fill in the “blank spots” of their own knowledge. Where the Sovietological enterprise went awry, however, was in making the transition from the details to the deeper dynamic driving Soviet reality.

zh: 简而言之，西方社会科学描绘的苏联是“现代性”的一个变体，无疑粗糙，但在相当程度上是成功的。大多数专家还一致认为，这个体制是“稳定的”；他们认为它构成国际事务两大极之一实属正常。此外（由于意识形态永远无法完全排除在价值中立的社会科学之外），许多专家还提出，苏联的“成熟工业社会”或许仍能实现其潜在的社会主义可能性。总之，呈现给我们的苏联体制是有生命力的、持久的，对某些人来说甚至大有希望——因此，显然我们都应当调整自己，永远与它共存。结果，没有人对它的骤然死亡做好准备。
en: Briefly put, the Soviet Union portrayed by Western social science represented a variant of “modernity,” rough-hewn no doubt, yet in significant measure a success. Most specialists agreed, further, that the system was “stable”; and they considered it normal that it should constitute one of the two great poles of international affairs. Moreover (since ideology could never be entirely excluded from value-free social science), many specialists suggested that the Soviet Union’s “mature industrial society” might yet realize its underlying socialist potential. In short, we were presented with a Soviet system that was viable, durable, and, for some, downright promising—and so it was clear that we should all adjust to living with it for good. In consequence, no one was prepared for the system’s brusque demise.

zh: 当然，指望任何人预测1989—1991年崩溃的确切形式，要求过高；自然也没有人做到。就连东欧的异见者，例如波兰团结工会的领导人，虽然始终看清这个体制的真实面貌，也在解放时刻到来时感到惊讶。但指望我们的解释范畴在共产主义崩溃发生后能够解释它，并不过分；而在这一点上，主流苏联学显然失败了。更糟的是，在崩溃之前，它的理论常常暗示、有时甚至明确预言与实际结果相反的情况。我们惯用的多数“模型”呈现给我们的苏联体制，即使不是永恒的，至少也是长久的：一个“城市的、工业的、受过教育的”社会，正如连祷文所说，像它的“资本主义”对手一样正常运转。诚然，一些观察者，特别是生活在体制下的异见者，确实察觉到它已病入膏肓、无法改革，但他们通常被社会科学苏联学置之不理。因此，几乎所有人，无论左派还是右派，都过于严肃地看待苏联的实力，无论把它当作理想还是对手。
en: Now, it would be too much to expect that anyone should have predicted the precise form of the crash of 1989-1991; and, of course, no one did. Even the dissidents of Eastern Europe, such as the leaders of Poland’s Solidarity, who all along saw the system as it really was, were surprised when the moment of their liberation came. But it is not too much to expect that our categories of explanation should be able to account for the collapse of Communism once it has occurred, and on this score mainstream Sovietology clearly fails. Worse still, before the collapse, its theories often intimated, and at times explicitly predicted, the opposite of the actual outcome. Most of our usual “models” presented us with a Soviet system which, although it might not be eternal, was at least permanent: an “urban, industrial, educated” society, as the litany went, that was as much a going concern as its “capitalist” adversary. To be sure, a number of observers, particularly dissidents living under the system, did perceive that it was too fatally flawed to be reformed, but they were usually dismissed by social-science Sovietology. Thus almost everyone, on both the Left and the Right, took Soviet prowess with too grim a seriousness, whether as an ideal or as an adversary.

zh: 为什么这么多人会在这么多事情上错这么久？最一般的答案不在苏联学本身，而在它借以观察研究对象的更广泛的社会科学文化。第二次世界大战后对苏联体制的系统研究开始之时，恰逢西方大学中所谓的行为主义革命。经济学、政治学、人类学和社会学这些学科，自19世纪和20世纪初不同时期起酝酿，终于在社会科学的独立院系和专业研究所中汇合，形成与自然科学和人文学科并列的第三大知识领域；这一发展也改造了历史悠久的历史学。所有这些学科都在某种程度上怀有使人与社会的研究尽可能精确和科学的抱负，这一事业非常符合奥古斯特·孔德的实证主义精神——当然，并不符合他的具体学说。这一学科武库的方法论很快被用于方兴未艾的苏联“社会”研究，结果就是我们所见到的不足。
en: How could so many have been so wrong about so much for so long? The most general answer is not to be found in Sovietology as such, but in the broader social-science culture through which it perceived its subject. The beginning of systematic study of the Soviet system in the wake of the Second World War coincided with what might be called the behavioral revolution in Western universities. The disciplines of economics, political science, anthropology, and sociology, in gestation since various times in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, at last came together in separate faculties of social science and in specialized research institutes to form a third great area of learning alongside the natural sciences and humanities; this development also transformed the venerable discipline of history. All of these disciplines shared, to some degree, the ambition of making the study of man and society as exact and as scientific as possible, an enterprise very much in the positivist spirit of Auguste Comte—though not, of course, in accordance with his precise doctrines. The methodologies of this arsenal of disciplines were soon brought to bear on the burgeoning study of Soviet “society” with the inadequate results that we have seen.

zh: 这种失败的第一个原因在于，我们所有伟大的社会科学理论都是在苏联体制出现之前设计的。先从马克思说起，没有比他关于社会分为占主导地位的社会经济基础和派生的政治文化上层建筑的划分，更容易误导对苏联现实的理解了，因为在苏联情况下，两者的关系恰恰颠倒。埃米尔·涂尔干尽管献身社会主义，他的“有机团结”和“道德”社会组织范畴作为对现代“失范”的答案，也帮不上更多忙。马克斯·韦伯虽然很清楚市场的重要性，却持有相当普鲁士式的观念，认为资本主义的本质是“法理型官僚制”：因此他预期，社会主义一旦到来，只会通过用超级官僚计划取代市场和私有财产，把理性的现代秩序再推进一步——充其量只说对了一半。
经典理论家中唯一与苏联经验真正相关的是亚历克西·德·托克维尔——但其中的原因要留待下一章。
en: A first reason for this failure is that all of our great social-science theories were devised before the Soviet system came on the scene. To begin with Marx, there is no more misleading guide to understanding Soviet realities than his division of society into a dominant socioeconomic base and a derivative political and cultural superstructure, since in the Soviet situation the relationship between the two is exactly reversed. Nor is Emile Durkheim, for all his commitment to socialism, any more helpful with his categories of “organic solidarity” and “moral” social organization as answers to modern “anomie.” Max Weber, though quite aware of the importance of the market, nonetheless held the rather Prussian idea that the essence of capitalism was “legal-rational bureaucracy”: he therefore expected that socialism, when and if its day came, would simply carry the rational modern order a step further by replacing the market and private property with hyperbureaucratic planning—at best a half-insight.
The only one of the classic theorists who is truly relevant to the Soviet experience is Alexis de Tocqueville—but the reasons for this must await the next chapter.

zh: 当20世纪早期到中期，伟大奠基者的工作被放大并制度化，形成学术社会科学时，应对苏联现象的情况并没有改善。部分原因是当时仍然相对稀少的苏联数据对新学科组合并不根本重要。但更重要的原因涉及新行为主义文化的基本前提。粗略地说，社会科学的观念假定：在具体社会形态的明显多样性背后，有一种叫作“社会”的东西是人类的基本现实，而这种“社会”在任何地方基本上都一样，过去如此，现在也如此。换句话说，尽管各文明在时间和地点上存在巨大差异，所有社会最终都受同样的结构、功能和发展的一般规律支配：否则就不可能有社会科学，而只有一堆临时观察的杂烩。
en: When, in the early to mid-twentieth century, the work of the great founders was amplified and institutionalized to produce academic social science, matters were not improved for coping with the Soviet phenomenon. In part this was because the still relatively sparse Soviet data were not fundamental to the new mix of disciplines. But the more important reason concerned the basic premise of the new behavioral culture. Crudely put, the idea of social science posits that, behind the obvious diversity of discrete social formations, something called “society” is the fundamental human reality, and that this “society” is basically the same everywhere, in the past no less than in the present. In other words, although there exist enormous differences in time and place among civilizations, all societies are ultimately governed by the same general laws of structure, function, and development: Were it otherwise, there could not be a science of society but only a jumble of ad hoc observations.

zh: 这一基本假设产生两个后果。第一，文化是一套“价值体系”，因此本质上是利益的函数；意识形态和政治因此是更基本的社会整体中的组成部分。马克思主义的上层建筑与经济基础二分法，只是这一视角的一种表达，尽管可能是最有影响的表达。因此，社会科学观念本身在某种程度上是还原论的：政治和意识形态只是“社会基础”的反映。第二，苏联发展的模式不可能是独特的或自成一格的，而必然与其他“现代”社会基本相似。这一观点再次把意识形态和政治置于社会过程之下。因此，社会科学苏联学在很大程度上把共产党政权宣称的“建设社会主义”目标斥为短暂的乌托邦主义或纯粹的宣传。正如一篇著名文章所说，苏联历史真正归结起来，是一个“从乌托邦到发展”的成熟过程。
en: Two consequences follow from this basic assumption. First, culture is a set of “value systems” and thus essentially a function of interests; ideology and politics, therefore, are subsets of the more basic global entity of society. The Marxist dichotomy between superstructure and base is simply one, albeit probably the most influential, expression of this perspective. Thus, the very idea of social science is in some measure reductionist: Politics and ideology are merely reflections of the “social base.” Second, the pattern of Soviet development cannot be unique or sui generis, but must be essentially similar to that of other “modern” societies. And this view, once again, subordinates ideology and politics to social process. Thus social-science Sovietology has largely dismissed the Communist regime’s declared goal of “building socialism” as transitory utopianism or mere propaganda. As one famous essay put it, what Soviet history really added up to was a process of maturation “from utopia to development.”

zh: 西方苏联学就这样把源自迥然不同的西方经验的范畴强加给苏联现实。列宁主义现象被歪曲了本来面目，奇异而超现实的苏联经验被弄得平庸到琐碎的地步。在大多数西方社会科学家眼中，苏联逐渐显得像“另一个社会”，与其他“现代”国家只有程度不同，没有性质不同。然而，真正现代化的国家不会像苏联体制在1989—1991年那样，因为一场单纯的改革而解体。本应成为现代史上重要社会科学案例的研究就这样被搞砸了，如今（但愿）将成为重新审视社会科学前提的起点。
en: In this manner, Western Sovietology proceeded to foist on Soviet reality categories derived from a very different Western experience. The Leninist phenomenon was denatured, and the fantastic and surreal Soviet experience was rendered banal to the point of triviality. In the eyes of most Western social scientists the Soviet Union came to appear as “just another society,” different only in degree, but not in kind, from other “modern” nations. However, genuinely modernized nations do not disintegrate as the result of a bout of mere reform as the Soviet system did in 1989-1991. What should have been the great social-science case study of the modern age thus was botched, and will now (hopefully) prove to be the starting point for a reexamination of social-science premises.

zh: 于是，社会科学的精致化最终把苏联现实弄得颠倒错乱。正如前苏联人常说的，他们的世界是一个“镜中世界”，是西方“资本主义”真正现代性的颠倒映像。或者，借用马克思对黑格尔唯心主义的描述，苏联体制是一个“颠倒的世界”，一个“头足倒立”的世界。也就是说，这是一个（与马克思自己的社会学相反）意识形态和政治构成体制的“基础”而非“上层建筑”的世界，是一个社会经济安排从作为基础的党派生而来的世界。因此，常识性的西方社会科学试图让苏联体制站在社会经济的双脚上，实际上却把它完全倒立起来。因此，本书的目标是把颠倒的苏联世界扶正，把它当作一个本质上颠倒的结构来处理。因为在十月创造的世界里，我们首先面对的从来不是一个
；我们始终面对的是一个意识形态统治的
en: And so social-science sophistication wound up getting Soviet reality backside to and upside down. As former Soviets used to say, their world was a “looking-glass world,” a reversed reflection of the real modernity of Western “capitalism.” Or, to adapt Marx’s characterization of Hegel’s idealism, the Soviet system was an “inverted world,” a world “standing on its head.” That is to say, it was a world where (contrary to Marx’s own sociology) ideology and politics formed the “base” of the system rather than its “superstructure,” and where socioeconomic arrangements derived secondarily from this Party base. Thus, commonsense Western social science, in its attempt to set the Soviet system on its socioeconomic feet, in fact stood it quite on its head. The aim of this book, therefore, is to set the inverted Soviet world right-side up by treating it as a structure that was by nature upside down. For in the world created by October we were never dealing in the first instance with a
rather, we were always dealing with an ideocratic

zh: 西方对苏维埃主义的颠倒视角，也许可以通过回顾西方苏联学史得到最好的说明。当严肃的苏联研究在第二次世界大战后、斯大林仍在克里姆林宫时开始时，理解苏维埃主义的问题显得严峻而简单。当时占主导的看法——它发展了流亡俄国自由主义史学家的立场——是：十月不是无产阶级革命，而是一个由组织严密、纪律严明的布尔什维克党实施的政变。这次少数人夺权之所以可能，只是因为第一次世界大战对帝俄摇摇欲坠的政治和社会结构造成了毁灭性冲击。因此，这场革命不是苏联马克思主义者所说的俄国历史过程逻辑的产物，而是对国家走向宪政民主的发展的粗暴中断。更具毁灭性的是，列宁的党专政按其逻辑导向斯大林主义，导向强制集体化和制度化的恐怖。
en: The West’s inverted perspective on Sovietism may be best illustrated by a look at the history of Western Sovietology. When serious Soviet studies got started in the wake of the Second World War, while Stalin was still in the Kremlin, the problem of understanding Sovietism appeared stark and simple. The prevailing view, which developed the positions of émigré Russian liberal historians, was this: October was not a proletarian revolution, but a coup d’état carried out by a monolithic and disciplined Bolshevik Party. This minority seizure of power was made possible only by the devastating impact of the First World War on the rickety political and social structures of Imperial Russia. The Revolution was therefore not a product of the logic of Russia’s historical processes, as Soviet Marxists would have it, but a brutal interruption of the country’s development towards constitutional democracy. More devastatingly still, Lenin’s Party dictatorship led logically to Stalinism, with its forced collectivization and institutionalized terror.

zh: 由于这些做法类似于同时代意大利和德国的“独裁政权”，“极权主义”一词——由墨索里尼以正面含义创造，用来指称他的新秩序，后由托洛茨基首次以负面含义用于斯大林俄国——被汉娜·阿伦特和其他纳粹主义难民采用，用来建立一种关于反常现代性和退化民主的一般理论。
他们这样做，是因为较为温和的“威权主义”一词——比如可用于萨拉查或蒋介石——根本不适合斯大林、希特勒或毛泽东那种令人毛骨悚然的宏大。
en: Since these practices resembled those of the contemporary “dictatorships” of Italy and Germany, the term “totalitarianism”—coined by Mussolini with a positive connotation to designate his new order and first applied in a negative sense to Stalin’s Russia by Trotsky—was taken up by Hannah Arendt and other refugees from Nazism to produce a general theory of perverse modernity and degenerate democracy.
And they did so because the blander term “authoritarian,” serviceable, say, for a Salazar or a Chiang Kai-shek, simply would not do for the gruesome grandeur of Stalin, Hitler, or Mao.

〔译注〕意大利反法西斯人士乔瓦尼·阿门多拉1923年已使用“极权的”一词批评法西斯政治；墨索里尼后来以正面含义使用该词。相关词形及其运用的历史比原书概括更复杂。

zh: 随后，随着赫鲁晓夫的去斯大林化，苏联开始显得更加平淡无奇；在1960年代，“极权主义模型”被现代化理论取代。这一视角——雷蒙·阿隆曾称之为“删去阶级斗争的马克思主义”——认为苏联政权在其社会主义辞藻和斯大林主义阴森道具背后，实际上是“发展”——工业化、城市化、大众教育——的力量，就像其他落后国家的“威权”政权一样。事实上，苏联案例可以被视为第三世界“发展经济学”的典范。一些专家甚至认为，苏俄有朝一日会与西方工业社会“趋同”，从而最终实现其民主潜能，并为新的混合体带来资本主义西方所缺乏的对人类需求的社会主义关切。或者，至少如果冷战的负担被解除，相应的意识形态辩护——“极权主义模型”及其将共产主义与纳粹主义诽谤性地等同——被驳倒，俄国就可能做到这一点。
en: Then, with Khrushchev’s de-Stalinization, the Soviet Union began to appear more prosaic; and in the course of the 1960s the “totalitarian model” was displaced by modernization theory. This perspective, which Raymond Aron once described as “Marxism with the class struggle left out,” held that the Soviet regime, behind its socialist rhetoric and the macabre trappings of Stalinism, was really a force for “development”—industrialization, urbanization, and mass education—like “authoritarian” regimes in other backward countries. Indeed, the Soviet case might be considered a model of “development economics” for the Third World. And some specialists even held that Soviet Russia would one day “converge” with Western industrial societies, thereby at last realizing its democratic potential and bringing to the new amalgam a socialist sensitivity to human needs that was lacking in the capitalist West. Or at least Russia might do this if the burden of the Cold War were lifted and the corresponding ideological justification—the “totalitarian model”—with its slanderous equivalence of Communism with Nazism, were refuted.

zh: 于是现代化理论逐渐转向一种更具意识形态色彩的视角，阶级斗争又蹑手蹑脚地回来了。然而，它却是踮着猫步悄悄回来的，因为这种新的社会经济路径平淡而学术化、实证主义化，回避一切公开的价值判断。这一新焦点部分归因于当时学术界的更大转向，即关注社会基础和普通人，这是历史视野的一次普遍富有成果的扩展，年鉴学派是最好的例证。然而，这一焦点的转移也归因于去斯大林化和缓和所带来的希望，以及军备控制需要一个可信的苏联伙伴。因此很快就显而易见：在现代化理论中，正如在极权主义模型中一样，对苏联实验那些充满价值的前提采取价值中立的态度，一如既往是自相矛盾的说法：总的来说，一个人要么支持幽灵，要么反对幽灵。
en: So modernization theory shaded off into a more ideological perspective, and the class struggle came creeping back in. It did so, however, on little cat feet, for this new socioeconomic approach was prosaically academic and positivistic, eschewing all overt value judgments. This new focus was in part due to a larger shift of scholarship at the time to a concern with the base of society and with ordinary people, a generally fruitful expansion of historical horizons best exemplified by the Annales school. The shift in focus was also due, however, to the hopes engendered by de-Stalinization and détente and to the need for a credible Soviet partner in arms control. So it soon became apparent that with modernization theory, no less than with the totalitarian model, a value-free approach to the value-laden pretensions of the Soviet experiment was as ever a contradiction in terms: Overall, one had to be either for or against the Specter.

zh: 因此，尽管1960年代和1970年代的新社会史有着严谨的实证外表，其中很大一部分实际上成了一种意识形态努力，试图把苏联体制解释为群众行动的产物，因而具有民主合法性。这就意味着对以国家为中心的极权主义模型的猛烈否定。由此产生的“修正主义”颠倒了其前任对政治和意识形态的强调，转而赋予社会和经济力量优先地位；它用“社会研究”取代“政权研究”，并声称要“从下面”解释苏联发展，把它视为社会的表达，而不是“从上面”解释为国家强加的结果。
en: Thus, for all its austere, empirical exterior, much of the new social history of the 1960s and 1970s in fact turned out to be an ideological effort to explain the Soviet system as the product of popular action, and hence as democratically legitimate. And this entailed a vehement repudiation of the state-centered totalitarian model. The resulting “revisionism” reversed its predecessor’s emphasis on politics and ideology, and gave priority instead to social and economic forces; it replaced “regime studies” with “social studies,” and purported to explain Soviet developments “from below,” as an expression of society, rather than “from above.” as an imposition of the state.

zh: 在这种新史学中，有两个主要问题至关重要。第一是政权的奠基行动即“伟大十月”本身作为无产阶级和社会主义革命的合法性。第二是列宁统治与斯大林统治之间是连续还是断裂的问题。这两个问题都进一步提出了斯大林之后苏联政权进行民主改革的能力问题——这也是一切地方社会主义的生命力问题。
en: In this new historiography two major issues were at stake. The first was the legitimacy of the founding act of the regime, “Great October” itself, as a proletarian and socialist revolution. The second was the question of continuity or discontinuity between Lenin’s rule and that of Stalin. And both issues posed the further question of the Soviet regime’s capacity for democratic reform after Stalin—which was also the question of the viability of socialism anywhere.

zh: 如果苏联政权起源于一场真正得到民众支持的革命，那么斯大林就是对列宁主义规范的“偏离”，体制因此有能力——尽管暂时绕道进入恐怖——回归民主和人道的社会主义。但如果这个体制诞生于一场阴谋政变，那么斯大林就是放大的列宁，就没有可以回归的民主源头：共产主义因此无法改革；它必须被废除。到1960年代末，英美史学大体上采纳了第一种即“乐观”视角，并因此围绕这些问题组织起来：哪里出了问题？什么时候出的错？怎样才能纠正？这种史学忽略了一种可能：这些可能是假问题；革命并没有
什么错，而是整个事业从一开始就
错的。
en: If the Soviet regime originated in a genuinely popular revolution, then Stalin was an “aberration” from the Leninist norm, and the system thus had the capacity, despite a temporary detour into horror, to return to democratic and humane socialism. But if the system was born in a conspiratorial coup, then Stalin was Lenin writ large, and there was no democratic source to return to: Communism therefore could not be reformed; it had to be abolished. By the late 1960s Anglo-American historiography had by and large adopted the first, or “optimistic,” perspective and was consequently organized around these questions: What went wrong? When did it go wrong? How might it be set right? This historiography ignored the possibility that these might be false questions: that nothing
wrong with the Revolution, but rather that the whole enterprise, quite simply,
wrong from the start.

zh: 因此，1960年代中期以后，苏联历史在西方被系统地按照“乐观的”社会视角重写。简而言之，这项工作的结论如下：十月是一场真正的无产阶级革命，由工人和资本家之间的阶级“极化”产生，而不是一场只有依靠第一次世界大战的“意外”才可能的少数人政变。
1917年的布尔什维克党不是铁板一块，而是缺乏纪律、多元的，因此是“民主的”。
列宁在1918—1921年战时共产主义时期诉诸恐怖和全面国有化，是内战紧急状态所必需的临时权宜之计；他真正的遗产是1920年代新经济政策（NEP）的“混合”经济，尼古拉·布哈林是他的合法继承人。
因此列宁主义不是极权主义的，斯大林被排除在布尔什维克历史的真正正典之外。事实上，共产主义现象的统一性干脆消失了，我们只剩下两个完全分离的实体：一方面是布尔什维主义和列宁主义，另一方面是斯大林主义，仿佛不存在党这样一个延续的制度，也不存在马克思列宁主义这样一种持久的世界观。
en: Thus after the mid-1960s Soviet history was systematically rewritten in the West from the “optimistic,” social perspective. Briefly, the conclusions of this endeavor run as follows: October was an authentic proletarian revolution, generated by class “polarization” between workers and capitalists, and not a minority coup d’état made possible only by the “accident” of the First World War.
The Bolshevik Party in 1917 was not monolithic, but instead undisciplined, diverse, and therefore “democratic.”

Lenin’s recourse to terror and to all-out nationalization during the War Communism of 1918-1921 were temporary expedients made necessary by the emergency of civil war; his true legacy was the “mixed” economy of the New Economic Policy, or NEP, of the 1920s, and Nikolai Bukharin was his legitimate heir.

Thus Leninism was not totalitarian, and Stalin was excluded from the authentic canon of Bolshevik history. Indeed, the unity of the Communist phenomenon simply disappeared, and we were left with two totally separate entities, Bolshevism and Leninism on the one hand, and Stalinism on the other, as if there were no such continuing institution as the Party and no such abiding worldview as Marxism-Leninism.

zh: 这至少是修正主义的主流，其核心要点是把列宁和十月与斯大林绝对分开。但还有一个更大胆的修正主义学派，认为斯大林主义如果得到正确理解并剪除某些过激之处，才是列宁主义的真正实现。这个学派认为，斯大林的第一个五年计划也有民主起源，其形式是党内和工人阶级内部针对留任的“资产阶级专家”的“文化革命”。此外，计划的后果是从工厂车间大规模“向上流动”，最终形成“勃列日涅夫一代”。在这种观点中，整个革命过程可以概括为“恐怖、进步和社会流动”，清洗受害者的总体代价不大，只有“几十万人中较低的数字”。
最后，这个成熟苏联的政治特征是具有“利益集团”相互作用的“制度多元主义”格局，就像所有其他“发达社会”一样。
en: This, at least, was the main current of revisionism, and its cardinal point was the absolute separation of Lenin and October from Stalin. But there was a bolder school of revisionism that suggested that Stalinism, properly understood and pruned of some of its excesses, was the real fulfillment of Leninism. This school held that Stalin’s first Five-Year Plan also had democratic origins, in the form of a “cultural revolution” from within the Party and the working class against holdover “bourgeois specialists.” Moreover, the consequence of the Plan was massive “upward mobility” from the factory floor that culminated in the “Brezhnev generation.” In this view the whole revolutionary process could be summed up as “terror, progress, and social mobility,” with the modest overall cost in purge victims falling in the “low hundreds of thousands.”
Finally, the politics of this mature Soviet Union was characterized by the interplay of “interest groups” in a pattern of “institutional pluralism,” just like in all other “developed societies.”

zh: 这第二个修正主义学派因此重新加入了极权主义模型对列宁与斯大林连续性的强调，不过对他们的同体性给予正面评价。但修正主义的两大主要支流在一个点上汇合：戈尔巴乔夫的
终将为苏联现代性大厦封顶，从而回归真正的十月，一切偏离都被克服，一切错误都被纠正。
en: This second revisionist school thus rejoined the totalitarian model’s emphasis on continuity between Lenin and Stalin, though with a positive evaluation of their consubstantiality. But the two principal strains of revisionism converged on one point: Gorbachev’s
would at last produce the crowning of the edifice of Soviet modernity, and thus a return to the True October, with all aberrations overcome and all wrong things set aright.

zh: 修正主义学术在崩溃前的二十五年里，主要就是围绕这些神学问题打转。在每一本新专著的导言中，极权主义模型都要受到仪式性的痛斥，“T字眼”（极权主义）被逐出礼貌的学术话语，使用它被视为几乎是在煽动对“邪恶帝国”的冷战敌意。到1985年
开始时，一片政治正确的阴霾已经笼罩了这个领域。
en: It is around these theological issues that revisionist scholarship largely turned during the two and one-half decades before the collapse. In the introduction to each new monograph, the totalitarian model was ritually excoriated, and the “T-word” was banished from polite academic discourse, its use viewed as virtual incitement to Cold War hostility towards the “Evil Empire.” By the onset of
in 1985, a pall of political correctness had settled over the field.

zh: 于是修正主义最终呈现给我们的，是一个几乎没有共产主义的20世纪俄国，一部没有王子的苏联《哈姆雷特》——也没有悲剧。
en: And so revisionism wound up by presenting us with a twentieth-century Russia virtually without Communism, a Soviet
without the prince—and also without the tragedy.

zh: 在1989—1991年的大崩溃之后，显然重新评估苏联学的基本假设和经典问题的时刻已经到来。要开辟这一新的研究方向，最好的起点是东方在苏联世界开始瓦解时出现的对共产主义的评价。具有讽刺意味的是，正当“极权主义”一词在1970年前后被从西方苏联学中清除时，它在东欧流行起来；汉娜·阿伦特的作品译文以

（地下抄本）形式传播，到1980年代末，一个曾在莫斯科被视为诽谤的标签，被苏联知识分子公开用来指称整个体制，包括其列宁主义阶段。事实上，戈尔巴乔夫本人在下台后也采用它来描述他试图取消的东西。诚然，1970年后这个禁忌词竟能被使用，这一事实本身就表明体制已不再是极权的了。因此，认识到这一明显事实，东欧知识分子区分了可以称为斯大林“高度极权主义”与勃列日涅夫“古典的”或常规的极权主义——用亚当·米赫尼克的话说，“被拔掉牙齿的极权主义”。
换句话说，他们采取历史的方法来定义这个棘手概念，认识到在共产主义下可以有重大变化而没有根本转变。
en: After the Great Collapse of 1989-1991, it is apparent that the time has come for a reappraisal of the basic assumptions and the classic problems of Sovietology. To make this new departure, the best place to begin is with the evaluation of Communism that emerged in the East once the Soviet world started to crumble. Ironically, just when the word “totalitarianism” was being expunged from Western Sovietology around 1970, it became current in Eastern Europe; Hannah Arendt was translated in

, and by the late 1980s, a label that was once considered calumny in Moscow was openly used by Soviet intellectuals to refer to the whole system, including its Leninist phase, Indeed Gorbachev himself, after his fall, adopted it to describe what he had been trying to undo. To be sure, the fact that after 1970 the forbidden term could be used at all indicated that the system was no longer total. So in recognition of this obvious fact, Eastern European intellectuals differentiated between what might be called the “high totalitarianism” of Stalin and the “classical,” or routine, totalitarianism of Brezhnev—“totalitarianism with its teeth kicked out,” in Adam Michnik’s phrase.
In other words, they took a historical approach to defining this vexed concept, recognizing that there could be significant change without fundamental transformation under Communism.

zh: 西方苏联学中关于极权主义的争论却没有这种细致入微之感，那里的辩论几乎浅薄得令人难堪。争论的起源在于斯大林去世时的形势。1956年，汉娜·阿伦特最初的历史和哲学路径被卡尔·J.弗里德里希和兹比格涅夫·布热津斯基编纂成一个抽象的“模型”。

他们用著名的六点把极权主义独裁定义为依赖于：(1)一套系统的意识形态，(2)一个单一群众党，(3)恐怖，(4)由现代技术支撑的传播垄断，(5)武器垄断，(6)中央控制的经济。所有这些当然都相当正确，尤其是对高度极权主义而言，尽管同样明显的是它并不穷尽。但这种描述也是静态的，部分因为社会科学模型本质上倾向于非历史的抽象，部分因为到斯大林统治末期体制事实上已经冻结。此外，一般极权主义模型没有充分区分左翼和右翼意识形态及其截然不同的效果。尽管如此，这个模型可以很容易地被历史化，在应用于具体情境时产生有价值的成果，特别是在梅尔·芬索德、伦纳德·夏皮罗和亚当·乌拉姆的著作中，这三位是极权主义路径最著名的经验实践者。
尽管如此，由于一般概念是静态的，它容易受到斯大林死后几十年苏联体制明显缓和这一事实的冲击。
en: No such sense of nuance marked the controversy over totalitarianism in Western Sovietology, where the debate was almost embarrassingly shallow. The origin of the controversy lay in circumstances as they stood at Stalin’s death. In 1956 the initial historical and philosophical approach of Hannah Arendt was codified and made into an abstract “model” by Carl J. Friedrich and Zbigniew Brzezinski.

In six famous points they defined totalitarian dictatorship as resting on (1) an elaborate ideology, (2) a single mass party, (3) terror, (4) a technologically conditioned monopoly of communication, (5) a monopoly of weapons, and (6) a centrally controlled economy. All of this, of course, is quite true, especially for high totalitarianism, though just as obviously it is not exhaustive. But this characterization is also static, in part because social-science models by their nature tend to ahistorical abstraction, and in part because the system by the end of Stalin’s reign had in fact become a frozen affair. In addition, the general totalitarian model does not distinguish adequately between ideologies of the Left and of the Right and their very different effects. Still, this model can easily be historicized to yield fruitful results when applied to concrete situations, as, notably, in the works of Merle Fainsod, Leonard Schapiro, and Adam Ulam, the three most notable empirical practitioners of the totalitarian approach.
All the same, since the general concept is static, it was vulnerable to the obvious mellowing of the Soviet system in the decades after Stalin’s death.

zh: 但修正主义在利用这一弱点时走得太远，在纠正一个错误时陷入了更糟的错误。这源于数量与质量之间，或者说苏维埃主义下控制程度与体制本身性质之间的概念混淆。因此，由于从斯大林到赫鲁晓夫和勃列日涅夫，镇压的范围和古拉格的规模急剧缩小，就得出了这样的结论：政权已经从极权主义演变为某种威权主义，比如上校统治下的希腊或皮诺切特的智利模式。于是，如果赫鲁晓夫和勃列日涅夫不能再像斯大林那样恐吓他们的经济管理者和军官，那么极权主义就让位于“多元主义”，铁板一块的党就变成了“利益”的“联盟”。
en: But revisionism went too far in exploiting this vulnerability, and in correcting one error it fell into a worse one. This resulted from a conceptual confusion between quantity and quality, or between the degree of control under Sovietism and the nature of the system as such. Thus, since the extent of repression and the dimensions of the Gulag shrank drastically from Stalin to Khrushchev and Brezhnev, the conclusion was drawn that the regime had evolved from totalitarianism to some form of authoritarianism, say, on the model of Greece under the colonels or of Pinochet’s Chile. And so, if Khrushchev and Brezhnev could no longer terrorize their economic managers and military officers as Stalin had, then totalitarianism had given way to “pluralism,” and the monolithic Party had become a “coalition” of “interests.”

zh: 诚然，斯大林之后的数量变化非常真实，而且对那些不得不在苏维埃主义下生活的人来说尤其令人欢迎。然而，这些变化并没有改变一个核心事实：基本结构依然完好：党国、中央计划和政治警察，通过各级党组织相互交错的领导网络运作，并由无处不在的鼓动宣传协调，整个体系服从于建设和保卫“现实社会主义”这一唯一压倒一切的目标。
en: To be sure, the quantitative changes after Stalin were most real and, what is more, especially welcome to those who had to live under Sovietism. Nevertheless, those changes did not alter the central fact that the fundamental structures remained intact: the Party-state, the central plan, and the political police, operating through an interlocking directorate of Party cells at every level and orchestrated by ubiquitous agitprop, the whole subordinated to the single overriding goal of building and defending “real socialism.”

zh: 东欧人挪用了西方抛弃的极权主义概念，用来指称正是这样一个总体体系。对他们来说，“极权的”并不意味着这类政权事实上对人口实行全面控制（因为这是不可能的）；相反，它意味着这种控制是它们的基本愿望。它并不意味着这类政权在表现上无所不能，而是说它们在制度结构上无所不包。简而言之，极权主义的不是苏联社会；而是苏联国家。因此，修正主义把火力主要对准了对极权主义概念的歪曲形象，实际上是对准了一个稻草人。结果是误解了共产主义的本质，用一个想象的、虚构的苏联取代了“现实存在”的那个东西。这远比极权主义模型高估体制对社会的控制程度或其持久能力要糟糕得多。
en: Eastern Europeans appropriated the cast-off Western concept of totalitarianism to designate just such a total system. For them, “totalitarian” did not mean that such regimes in fact exercised total control over the population (since this is impossible); instead, it meant that such control was their basic aspiration. It did not mean that such regimes were omnipotent in performance, but rather that they were omnicompetent in their institutional structure. In short, it was not Soviet society that was totalitarian; rather, it was the Soviet state. Thus revisionism largely directed its fire against a caricature of the totalitarian concept, indeed against a straw man. The result was to misconstrue the essence of Communism and to put an imaginary, make-believe Soviet Union in the place of the “really existing” article. And this was far worse than the totalitarian model’s overestimation of the extent of the system’s control over society, or of the degree of its staying power over time.

zh: 这场术语之争也不只是标签问题。斯大林之后东欧和苏联异见的一个主要主题，是把语言从党的意识形态词典中解放出来。对俄国的索尔仁尼琴来说，正如对波兰的亚当·米赫尼克来说，解放社会的第一步是“拒绝按照谎言生活”，用事物的真实名称而不是意识形态委婉语来称呼它们。同样，“威权主义”、“多元主义”、“发展型独裁”以及诸如此类的社会科学称谓，对于苏联共产主义这个非凡的总体现象来说都严重不足。这一现象的独特性迫切需要一种单独而独特的称呼，而20世纪的粗粝经验已经给了我们这样一个词。它就是极权主义。使用任何更弱、更稀释的名称，都是改变现实的本来面貌，歪曲我们所谈论的对象。
en: Nor is this quarrel over terminology a mere matter of labels. One of the major themes of Eastern European and Soviet dissidence after Stalin was the liberation of language from the ideological lexicon of the Party. For Solzhenitsyn in Russia, as for Adam Michnik in Poland, the first step toward the liberation of society was to “refuse to live according to the lie,” to call things by their real names and not by their ideological euphemisms. Similarly, “authoritarianism,” “pluralism,” “developmental dictatorship,” and

social-science designations are grossly inadequate for the extraordinary, total phenomenon of Soviet Communism. The uniqueness of this phenomenon cries out for a separate and distinct designation, and the rude experience of the twentieth century has given us such a term. It is totalitarianism. To use any lesser, diluted name is to denature reality and to misrepresent what we are talking about.

zh: 同样，而且再次与东欧舆论一致，苏维埃主义必须被视为从十月开始的一个统一体，视为某种与之前任何事物——无论俄国还是西方——根本不同的东西。它在时间上独特，在社会类型学上也独特。这种独特性通过其消亡的非凡方式，被昔日的苏维埃主义臣民深切体会。第一，崩溃的总体性——意识形态、政治、经济——仿佛一个总体体系只能以总体崩溃告终。第二，这场崩溃产生的全面否定；所有制度——党、计划、警察——所有圣像，一直追溯到列宁和十月，都被明确贬斥和否定。到处都能听到人们希望回归“正常社会”。
en: By the same token, and again in accordance with Eastern European opinion, Sovietism must be seen as a unity from October onward, and as something radically different from anything that preceded it, whether in Russia or in the West. It is as unique in time as it is in the typology of societies. This uniqueness was borne home to the erstwhile subjects of Sovietism by the extraordinary manner of its demise. First, there was the totality of the collapse—ideological, political, economic—as if a total system could only end in total collapse. Second, there was the totality of the repudiation this collapse produced; all the institutions—Party, plan, police—all the icons, right back to Lenin and October, were explicitly deprecated and repudiated. And on all sides one heard that people wanted to return to a “normal society.”

zh: 但这当然等于说，在过去七十多年里，他们生活在一个不正常的社会中，即“发达社会主义”的制度化幻影，实际上是一个荒诞的社会剧场。这种苏联经验的奇幻性质之感，也许是伟大“苏联”文学的中心主题：对于明确的奇幻大师（沿着果戈理的方式），如米哈伊尔·布尔加科夫、安德烈·普拉东诺夫、阿布拉姆·特尔茨和亚历山大·季诺维耶夫，这显然是真的；对于安娜·阿赫玛托娃和奥西普·曼德尔施塔姆这样的新古典主义者也是如此，他们的作品在崩溃之际也都充分获得应有的地位并得以公开出版。
en: But this, of course, was tantamount to saying that for the previous seventy-odd years they had lived in an abnormal society, the institutionalized phantasmagoria of “developed socialism” that was in fact a social theater of the absurd. And this sense of the fantastic quality of the Soviet experience is perhaps the central theme of the greatest “Soviet” literature: This is obviously true of the explicit masters of the fantastic (after the manner of Gogol), such as Mikhail Bulgakov, Andrei Platonov, Abram Tertz, and Aleksandr Zinoviev; it is also true of such neoclassicists as Anna Akhmatova and Osip Mandelshtam, all of whose writings came fully into their own and into open legality at the moment of the collapse.

zh: 从这个视角看，应当显而易见：过去七十年里，俄国绝不是另一个现代化国家。相反，它是西方历史上第一次尝试把“乌托邦置于权力之中”的非凡冒险。
当然，乌托邦从未实现，但这不是重点。因为应用乌托邦不会简单地失败并消退；通过意外后果的规律，它们反而导致现实的一幅怪诞的漫画——一种超现实。
en: Seen in this perspective, it should be apparent that for the past seven decades Russia has been anything but just another modernizing country. It has been, rather, the extraordinary adventure, for the first time in Western history, of attempting to put “utopia in power.”

The utopia, of course, was never realized, but this is not the point. For applied utopias do not simply fail and fade away; through the law of unintended consequences, they lead, rather, to the emergence of a monstrous caricature of reality—a surreality.

zh: 因此，苏联实验的结果最好被理解为黑格尔所谓“理性的狡计”的反常显现，他指的是历史行动者在自己不知不觉中被事件的“逻辑”有目的地引导。所以列宁主义的冒险变成了所谓的“哥伦布的错误”：党扬帆驶向社会主义，却意外撞上了苏维埃主义，从而把俄国带入了颠倒的现代性。但这一未预见的登陆确实导致了一种新政治、新经济以及（几乎）新苏联人的出现。这确实是一项“世界历史性”成就，如黑格尔可能会说的，尽管不是他的门徒马克思和列宁所期待的那一项。
en: The outcome of the Soviet experiment, therefore, is best understood as a perverse manifestation of what Hegel called the “cunning of reason,” by which he meant that historical actors are unwittingly yet purposefully led by a “logic” of events of which, they themselves are unaware. So the Leninist adventure turned out to be what has been called a “mistake of Columbus”: the Party set sail for socialism but instead stumbled on Sovietism, thereby landing Russia in an inverted modernity. But this unforeseen landfall did, in fact, lead to the creation of a new politics, a new economics, and (almost) a new Soviet man. And this was indeed a “world-historical” achievement, as Hegel might have put it, though not the one that his disciples Marx and Lenin anticipated.

zh: 只有从这种悖论出发，才能在最深层次上理解苏联历史。因为前苏联虽然显然是一个失败的乌托邦，却既不是一个发达也不是一个现代国家。相反，它是某种自成一格的东西，一种在性质上与本世纪或此前各世纪一切专制形式都不同的现象。
en: It is only in terms of this paradox that Soviet history can be understood at its deepest level. For the former Soviet Union, though clearly a failed utopia, was neither a developed nor a modern nation. It was, rather, something sui generis, a phenomenon qualitatively different from all other forms of despotism in this or in previous centuries.

zh: 但这一事实把我们带回已经指出的悖论：直到最后，大部分苏联学看到的都是一个相当不同的苏联，其总账是正面的。因此我们面对一个最终且更深的问题：苏联人怎么能在众目睽睽之下，如此长久地蒙混过关，而这场实验从一开始就是一场世界历史性的骗局？他们又怎么能如此长久地自欺，以为布尔什维克的奇幻事业已经产生了“资本主义”的世界历史性替代品？事实上，这场实验的最高悖论是：西方历史上从未有过如此巨大的失败，同时又是如此不可抗拒的成功。
en: But this fact returns us to the already noted paradox that until the very end most Sovietology saw a quite different Soviet Union, one whose balance sheet was, overall, positive. So we are confronted with a final and still deeper problem: How could the Soviets get away for so long, and in full view of the outside world, with what turned out to have been from the start a world-historical fraud? And how could they deceive themselves for so long that the fantastic enterprise of Bolshevism had produced the world-historical alternative to “capitalism”? Indeed, the supreme paradox of the experiment is that never before in Western history has such a monumental failure been such an irresistible success.

zh: 然而，所有这些悖论的解决办法出奇地简单。十月置于权力之中的乌托邦，是现代的意识形态共同财产，这场实验不仅为俄国，而且为全人类而进行。因为如果苏俄只是一次发展落后国家的尝试，它就绝不会迷住世界。因此，西方观察者在写作苏联经验时，总是在间接评论自己的社会，同时把西方的政治关切投射到苏联现实上。这种情况只会强化社会科学文化把苏维埃主义与地球其余部分同质化的方法论倾向。因此，在苏联学辩论的实证主义外表背后，往往潜伏着对普世社会主义荣誉的关切。这种关切，不亚于发展模型，产生了相信“实验”有朝一日终将一切顺利的压力。
en: Yet, the solution to all of these paradoxes is surprisingly simple. The utopia that October put in power was the ideological common property of the modern age, and the experiment was conducted not just for Russia, but for all mankind. For if Soviet Russia had only been an exercise in developing a backward country, it never would have mesmerized the world. Thus, in writing about the Soviet experience, Western observers were always indirectly commenting on their own society, and at the same time projecting Western political concerns onto Soviet reality. And this circumstance only reinforced the methodological propensity of social-science culture to homogenize Sovietism with the rest of the planet. Thus, behind the positivistic exterior of the Sovietological debate more often than not there lurked a concern for the honor of universal socialism. And this concern, no less than the developmental model, generated pressure to believe that the “experiment” would, someday, have to turn out all right.

zh: 这种乌托邦希望的永恒回归，穿透了社会科学严谨性的门面，把我们带回这样一个前提：理解苏联现象的关键是意识形态。只有按苏联人的意识形态话语来理解他们，认真地按字面理解他们的社会主义乌托邦，我们才能把握它所导致的悲剧。
en: This eternal return of utopian hope, breaking through the facade of social-science rigor, brings us back to the premise that the key to understanding the Soviet phenomenon is ideology. It is only by taking the Soviets at their ideological word, treating their socialist utopia with literal-minded seriousness, that we can grasp the tragedy to which it led.

zh: 因此，本书的具体议程是：在理解苏联现象时，重申意识形态和政治对社会经济力量的优先性。以“自上而下”而非“自下而上”的视角重新解释苏联发展的动力。最后，是复活极权主义视角，但以一种历史的、动态的而非静态的方式；因为正是苏联乌托邦无所不包的抱负，提供了只能被称为悲剧“遗传密码”的东西。
en: The concrete agenda of this book, therefore, is to reassert the primacy of ideology and politics over social and economic forces in understanding the Soviet phenomenon. It is to rehabilitate history “from above” at the expense of history “from below” as the motive force of Soviet development. Finally, it is to resurrect the totalitarian perspective, but in a historical and dynamic, not a static, mode; for it was the all-encompassing pretensions of the Soviet utopia that furnished what can only be called the “genetic code” of the tragedy.

zh: 因此，接下来的各章将首先关注分析和解释。必要的事件叙述不打算面面俱到，而是为了证实基本论点。此外，叙述在苏联历史早期和后期之间的详细程度会有所不同。1917—1939年的事件在西方史学中已被最彻底地勾勒出来，因此在这里需要最少的重述。1939年以后，尤其是勃列日涅夫时期，叙述将逐渐更完整，因为我们仍在拼凑这一时期的基本轮廓；而对结构尚不清晰的戈尔巴乔夫终局，叙述将最为完整。
en: Thus the chapters that follow will be concerned in the first instance with analysis and interpretation. The necessary accompanying narrative of events is not intended to be comprehensive, but, rather, to substantiate the basic argument. The narrative, moreover, will vary in detail between the earlier and later periods of Soviet history. The events of the years 1917-1939 have been the most thoroughly staked out in Western historiography and hence will require the least retelling here. The narrative will become progressively fuller after 1939, and especially with the Brezhnev years, since we are still piecing together the basic contours of this period; and the narrative will be fullest of all for the as yet poorly structured Gorbachev finale.

zh: 最后一点方法论说明：这项研究将大量谈论苏维埃主义的“逻辑”。但为了避免有人喊“决定论”，应当解释，这里使用的这个词是相当普通的意义，就像我们谈论市场的逻辑、核军备的逻辑或有竞争的选举的逻辑——即特定情境的逻辑，而不是历史本身的逻辑。因为如果我们不能谈论这种有界限的逻辑，我们就根本无法对历史作出任何有意义的论述。
en: A concluding methodological word: This investigation will have much to say about the “logic” of Sovietism. But lest anyone cry “determinism,” it should be explained that the term is employed here in a quite ordinary sense, as when we speak of the logic of the market, or of nuclear armaments, or of contested elections—that is, the logic of a given situation as opposed to the Logic of History itself. For if we could not speak of such circumscribed logics, we could not say anything meaningful about history at all.

zh: 然而，在这项探究中，还涉及一种更广泛、更长期（但不是形而上学）的逻辑。这是现代的自明逻辑，自启蒙运动和法国大革命首次让人们产生历史具有世俗目标或目的的观念以来，这个时代就被如此定义——这一观念通常被称为进步。这种进步模式有两个主要方面：第一，历史通向人类对自然的理性、科学征服；第二，历史通向一个理性、平等的社会。苏联实验本应是这种进步逻辑的顶点；这当然结果是一场幻觉。但这种幻觉之所以可能，无论东方还是西方，只是因为历史
在朝着更大的平等和科学能力不断加速前进。正是把这种双重运动意识形态化为社会主义，才使苏联实验成为可能。
en: However, in this inquiry, a broader and more long-term (though not metaphysical) logic is also involved. It is the self-evident logic of the modern age, as that age has been defined since the Enlightenment and the French Revolution first gave men the idea that history had a secular goal, or telos—a notion generally referred to as progress. And this pattern of progress had two main aspects: First, history was leading to man’s rational, scientific mastery of nature, and second, it was leading to a rational, egalitarian society. The Soviet experiment was supposed to be the culmination of this logic of progress; and this of course turned out to be an illusion. But this illusion was possible, both in the East and in the West, only because history was

in constantly accelerating movement towards greater equality and scientific prowess. It was the ideological hypostasis of this dual movement as Socialism that alone made possible the Soviet experiment.

zh: 因此，本项探究的相关基本概念不是现代化，甚至也不是极权主义；而是社会主义。理解我们的故事不需要任何其他“模型”。
en: Thus, the relevant basic concept of the present inquiry is not modernization or even totalitarianism; it is socialism. No other “model” is required to understand our story.
